subtopic: Sparse vs dense kernel boundary / When sparsity pays
learningObjective: Identify when unstructured or structured sparsity actually reduces wall-clock time on GPU, vs when it only reduces FLOP count.

hardwareContext.architecture: Ampere or newer for 2:4 sparse tensor cores

stem: Select all statements that correctly characterize the boundary between sparse and dense GPU kernels. (Choose all that apply.)

options.text: Any percentage of sparsity greater than 50% in a weight matrix automatically gives a proportional wall-clock speedup on modern GPUs, since sparse tensor-cores dynamically skip zero tiles regardless of the sparsity pattern.

Unstructured sparsity (arbitrary zero pattern) rarely translates to wall-clock speedup on GPU unless density is well below ~10%, because indexing overhead and irregular memory access outweigh the FLOP reduction on tensor-core-driven dense hardware.
Structured 2:4 sparsity delivers a real ~2x speedup on any dtype and any GEMM shape, since the Sparse Tensor Core hardware is dtype- and shape-agnostic once the mask is applied.

For LLM inference, weight sparsity that reduces HBM traffic (e.g., N:M or block-sparse weight formats) is more impactful than FLOP reduction, because decode is bandwidth-bound. However, this only works if a compatible sparse kernel exists for the target dtype.

explanation: Options B, D are correct; options A, C are incorrect. A (Wrong): hardware requires the 2:4 structure; arbitrary sparsity does not get hardware-native skipping. B (Correct): unstructured sparsity break-even point on GPU is very low density. C (Wrong): Wrong (as stated): 2:4 does provide speedup but only on supported dtypes and with dedicated kernels; the option's blanket 'yields real speedup' is unconditional and misleading. D (Correct): decode is bandwidth-bound; sparsity that reduces HBM traffic can help if a kernel exists.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: hardware requires the 2:4 structure; arbitrary sparsity does not get hardware-native skipping.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: unstructured sparsity break-even point on GPU is very low density.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong as stated: while structured 2:4 sparsity on Ampere+ Sparse Tensor Cores can deliver up to ~2x GEMM speedup, this is scoped to (a) supported dtypes (FP16 / BF16 / INT8 / TF32 on A100; FP8 added on H100), (b) sufficiently large M/N/K so the sparse path is dispatched, and (c) accuracy-preserving pruning of the weight to the 2:4 pattern. The blanket 'any dtype and any GEMM shape' claim is an overclaim.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: decode is bandwidth-bound; sparsity that reduces HBM traffic can help if a kernel exists.

assumptions: GPU refers to modern NVIDIA GPUs (Ampere and newer).
'Sparse kernel' means a specialized kernel that reads only nonzeros and their indices.
nonImplications: Does not imply that sparsity never helps; it does at extreme sparsity or with structured formats.
Does not imply block-sparse and 2:4 are equivalent; they trade regularity for compression differently.

performanceClaim.scope: Sparse vs dense wall-clock speedup on GPU
